class.name: FellowBurnable3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: makes a [MeshInstance3D] burn like wood: it chars, glows, recedes and ends as ash, its volatiles feeding the flames of a [FellowGasVolume3D].
class.description: The mesh of [member mesh_path] (empty: the parent) is voxelized ([member resolution] voxels along its longest side); each voxel has a temperature and how much of it is wood, char and ash. The GPU heats the voxels from the gas around the object (the flames' temperature, by convection and radiation) or from the surface's own flame (over the wood that is burning, climbing [member flame_reach] above it at [member flame_temperature]: what keeps the object burning on its own), conducts the heat inwards, pyrolyses the wood to char (above [member pyrolysis_temperature]; the volatiles become the gas's fuel, so the visible flames come from the object itself), oxidises the exposed char to ash (above [member glow_temperature]: glowing embers) and lets the remains (the ash, and the char where it has crumbled) fall to the ground below and slide into a heap, still glowing while hot. Once less than [member collapse_fraction] of the wood and char is left, the object's physics body stops colliding (signal [signal collapsed]). Thin parts burn through first, thick ones char slowly. The mesh is drawn from the voxels: its vertices recede with the material, its surface darkens with char and greys with ash, and the hot char glows in its cracks; where it has burned through it is not drawn, and the ash and the crumbled charcoal are drawn as a heap of their own (an internal child mesh instance, [code]FellowAshHeap[/code], added when the first ash appears). The gas flows around the object's voxels (its physics body is not the gas's obstacle). Runs only in a running game, not in the editor. While in the tree it replaces the mesh instance's mesh (subdivided so the surface can follow the voxels) and its materials ([BaseMaterial3D] and [ShaderMaterial] spatial shaders are extended with the burning); they are restored when it leaves. Needs a RenderingDevice renderer (Forward+ or Mobile). Without a gas volume an object lit by [method ignite] burns by its own flame, without visible flames. At most 8 burning objects inject into one gas volume. See [code]docs/decisions/0120-burning.md[/code].
